Mathilde Pedersen is a quality consultant and a representative for the data controller authority (SundK) within the Danish healthcare system. She serves as a member of the [[styregruppen-for-danibd|Styregruppen for DANIBD]], the steering committee for the Danish National Quality Database for Inflammatory Bowel Disease [^src1]. 

Her role on the committee underscores the database's institutional focus on quality management, methodological validity, and regulatory compliance regarding health data governance [^src1]. The steering committee is an interdisciplinary and regional group comprising doctors, nursing leaders, patient representatives, and experts from the Danish Healthcare Quality Institute (Sundhedsvæsenets Kvalitetsinstitut) [^src1]. As the representative for the data controller authority, Pedersen is part of the governance framework that oversees DANIBD's operations, which include maintaining a validated data coverage rate of over 90% and supporting national quality measurement and benchmarking in IBD care [^src1].
